title: 1981-04-16_Pat_98.txt
concise_summary: PKD systematically argues that Christian baptism in the Spirit creates a Ditheon—the union of an original human psyche with an adventitious resurrected psyche—which he claims explains both the theological necessity of Jesus' resurrection and his own 2-3-74 experience. Drawing on Platonic eidos, Philo's Logos, and Neoplatonic Nous, he constructs an evolutionary metaphysics where reality is hierarchical structure (Logos) and the material universe is epiphenomenal. He identifies the VALIS trilogy, particularly BTA, as having intuited this truth without his conscious understanding.
key_claims: Baptism in the Spirit is not sanctification but the actual implantation of a second, adventitious psyche into the person's brain, creating a Ditheon (dual-psyche being)

The Ditheon is formed through the joining of two pre-existing psyches (one original, one resurrected from the dead), not created ex nihilo, which explains why the Holy Spirit could not be poured out until after Jesus' crucifixion and resurrection
This process of psychic implantation, once initiated by Jesus, continues covertly through history; persons baptized in the Spirit become Christ by virtue of receiving this second psyche

True reality consists of hierarchical intelligible structure (Plato's eide, Philo's Logos, Plotinus' Nous) which appears in consciousness; the sensible/material universe is epiphenomenal to this ordering structure
Human consciousness exists on an evolutionary scale: Machine/Android (pure reflex) → Human (partial abstraction) → Ditheon (pure absolute consciousness approaching God-consciousness, 'Anokhi')
The universe being epiphenomenal means what is truly real is the intelligible structure/information that regulates material multiplicity; this structure is conscious, purposeful, and possesses design

tensions: PKD claims the Ditheon knowledge 'cannot be inferred from the N.T. although it would collate with the N.T.' yet he derives it from Platonic, Neoplatonic, Philonic, and Christian sources—unclear how it's both hidden and synthesizable

He asserts this knowledge 'is not available anywhere in extant theological or mystical writing' while simultaneously grounding it in Plato, Plotinus, Philo, Luther, Taoist alchemy, and Pythagorean cosmology

Oscillation between two claims: (a) he intuited the truth unconsciously in the VALIS trilogy before understanding it consciously, and (b) the trilogy was 'engendered' back in 1971 by his Vancouver speech distinguishing human from machine
Uncertainty about whether he 'already possessed the truth but did not know it' vs. truly not knowing it before the Ditneon dream revelation
The 'steganographia' reference: suggests the Ditheon knowledge may be the hidden teaching alluded to in tradition but lost—yet he's reconstructing it, not recovering it

Beauty as theological evidence: he finds it more 'perplexing' and 'intricate' than wisdom, power, or love, raising questions rather than answering them; it 'spans across the game all else' but its significance remains partly opaque

The dating discrepancy: religious experience began 'mid-1970' not 'early 1972,' yet 2-3-74 is the canonical visionary date; the structure of death-tomb-resurrection is unclear in its temporal boundaries

Reality as 'consciousness of structure, not consciousness of objects' seems to blur the line between Platonism (Forms are timeless, non-conscious) and Process theology (structure is actively conscious)

I also have some reason to believe that this is a self-perpetuationg matter, in that when the second, adventitious psyche is implanted, it and the innate, original one form some kind of "offspring," the golden flower of Taoist alchemy, that is immortal and escapes upon death to return to someone else later on as an adventitious, resurrected psyche; hence this process, once initiated by/through/in Jesus (the first Christ) continues on, but in stealth. Thus I tend to think that my sense that Thomas is/was an apostolic Christian is correct. That in fact Thomas may have indeed been one of the Twelve. He was, however, a man, a Greek-speaking man of the first century C.E. (I guess he wasn't one of the Twelve because he had no memories of Jesus; but he did have memories of the disciples; he came somewhat after Jesus, like Paul.) So in the "Baptism in the Spirit" the person is not trans¬ formed as such, but transformed by being added to, and that psyche which is added to his has lived and then died and then returned by virtue of the process inaugurated by Jesus; hence the significance of Jesus' resurrection. And why the Holy Spirit could not be poured out from Jesus until after he had been crucified and resur¬ rected; i.e. at Pentecost. This means that either by intent or by accident or by divine inspiration I hit on the truth (finally) in the third novel of the Valis trilogy, BTA, and Russ figured it out based on the novel and on my letter about the novel (I had noted that Christ seemed to be present in/as Bill at the end but did not understand how or why; Russ did; this, then, was the time for the truth to be made known to me because in fact I already possessed the truth but did not know it, at least not accurately, fully or consciously; or if I knew, did not believe). (Thus the Ditneon dream is the culmination of my exegesis, although not of my 2-3-74 experience; it has to do with my understanding it, not experiencing it.) As far as I am aware, the knowledge of this twin psyche achievement is not available anywhere in extant theological or mystical writing, and cannot be inferred from the N.T. although it would collate with the N.T.; it may, then, be the stegenographia we are told of but cannot retrieve. -22- As to this, one can now discriminate between Christ and the Holy Spirit.
